meta.title: A Gelatin Methacrylate-Based Hydrogel as a Potential Bioink for 3D Bioprinting and Neuronal Differentiation.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Four GelMA-based bioinks were compared for printing human iPSC-derived neural progenitors and SH-SY5Y cells. A 4% GelMA ink kept cells viable, printed easily, and supported differentiation into immature neurons.

formulations.name: 4% GelMA (4GMA)
formulations.key_outcome: 4% GelMA was chosen for keeping cells viable with good printability; printed hNPCs became immature neurons.

evidence.quote: we selected the 4GMA_Gx composition for further bioprinting assays
Cells were bioprinted using a 3DBS Educational Starter Printer, which produced constructs measuring 4 × 4 × 1 mm.
The stiffness of the four bioinks presented in this work are 5 to 45 kPa and thus within that range.
